messages.subject: How do I get an estimate for % explained variance from scantwo-output?
messages.subject_clean: How do I get an estimate for % explained variance from scantwo-output?
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I'm interested in how I can get an estimate of the percentage of explained variance from a scantwo-output? Should I apply simply the formula: % explained variance = 100 ( 1 - 10^(-2 LOD / n) )?
Secondly, what's the difference between the epistatic interaction and the conditional interaction? Should I finally sum up the derived values for the % explained variance from the three columns for joint LOD, epistatic LOD and conditional LOD?

I tried to use makeqtl and fitqtl to get an estimate of QTL effects.
E.g., I've detected four QTL in a 10 cM interval interacting with the same QTL on chromosome 5. I've included every single QTL on chromosome 1 and the QTL on chromosome 5 in the QTL model, but the LOD scores in the summaryfitqtl-output differed from the LOD output from scanqtl.
Currently, I have no idea what the error of reasing might be, for instance in formulating the genetic model or in the general procedure within R/qtl from scantwo to fitqtl etc?
I would be very happy if someone could give me some advice!
Regards
Christof

Gene and Genome Mapping
Dept. Cytogenetics
Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Resarch Gatersleben
Corrensstrasse 3
D-06466 Gatersleben
Germany

messages.subject: Re: How do I get an estimate for % explained variance from scantwo-output?
messages.subject_clean: How do I get an estimate for % explained variance from scantwo-output?
messages.body_plain:
On Sep 4, 2006, at 8:22 AM, Christof Pietsch IPK wrote:

> Dear all,
> I'm interested in how I can get an estimate of the percentage of
> explained variance from a scantwo-output? Should I apply simply the
> formula: % explained variance = 100 ( 1 - 10^(-2 LOD / n) )?

You could use that formula with the joint LOD score and it would
indicate the
estimated percent variance explained by the pair of QTL.

> Secondly, what's the difference between the epistatic interaction
> and the conditional interaction? Should I finally sum up the
> derived values for the % explained variance from the three columns
> for joint LOD, epistatic LOD and conditional LOD?

As explained in the help file for plot.scantwo, the cond-int LOD
score compares the joint likelihood to the best of the two single-
locus likelihoods.  The epistatic LOD score compares the joint
likelihood to the likelihood for two additive QTL.

> I tried to use makeqtl and fitqtl to get an estimate of QTL effects.
> E.g., I've detected four QTL in a 10 cM interval interacting with
> the same QTL on chromosome 5. I've included every single QTL on
> chromosome 1 and the QTL on chromosome 5 in the QTL model, but the
> LOD scores in the summaryfitqtl-output differed from the LOD output
> from scanqtl.
> Currently, I have no idea what the error of reasing might be, for
> instance in formulating the genetic model or in the general
> procedure within R/qtl from scantwo to fitqtl etc?

scanqtl simply calls fitqtl repeatedly, with the locations of QTL
allowed to vary across an interval.
The function is essentially without documentation at this point, but
we hope to rectify that soon.
It's output contains the joint LOD scores for the multiple-QTL models.

karl

messages.subject: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.subject_clean: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl (and anyone else who can help),

I have a few questions about obtaining QTL effect estimates and the
analysis of dominant data in r/qtl.  I am analyzing an F2 intercross
using primarily dominant AFLP markers and we have a X0
sex-determination system.

1. Am I correct in my understanding that fitqtl and other procedures
using the impumentation method take into account missing data (e.g.
genotype of indivudals with dominant allele at a dominant locus) by
analyzing simulated genotypes (i.e. sim.geno) based on estimated
genotype probabilities (i.e. calc.genoprob) calculated from the linkage
map and an estimate of the error rate?

2. Is there a way to estimate the effect of X-linked QTL based on
multiple impumentation in r/qtl. I am aware that fitqtl can not
currently handle X-linked data from an F2 intercross, but is there some
work-around that you could suggest that would provide comparable
results to those for autosomal QTL?

3. I have used fitqtl to estimate the additive and dominant effect of
autosomal QTL; however, I am not clear how the additive and dominant
effects of QTL linked to dominant loci are estimated by fitqtl. Is
estimation of additive and dominant effects for QTL linked to dominant
loci dependent upon estimation of genotype probabilities based on
linked codominant markers? If so, how should the fitqtl effect
estimates for QTL from linkage groups with only dominant loci be
interpreted?

Thanks for your help,
sky

messages.subject: Re: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.subject_clean: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.body_plain:
On Sep 28, 2006, at 12:43 PM, sky wrote:

>
> Hi Karl (and anyone else who can help),
>
> I have a few questions about obtaining QTL effect estimates and the
> analysis of dominant data in r/qtl.  I am analyzing an F2 intercross
> using primarily dominant AFLP markers and we have a X0
> sex-determination system.

The procedures in R/qtl were developed for an XY sex-determination
system, but I suppose that XO behaves similarly, and so things should
work.

> 1. Am I correct in my understanding that fitqtl and other procedures
> using the impumentation method take into account missing data (e.g.
> genotype of indivudals with dominant allele at a dominant locus) by
> analyzing simulated genotypes (i.e. sim.geno) based on estimated
> genotype probabilities (i.e. calc.genoprob) calculated from the
> linkage
> map and an estimate of the error rate?

fitqtl uses (at this point) exclusively multiple imputation; such
imputations are obtained by sim.geno.  The results of calc.genoprob
are used by the other methods.

All methods except marker regression (method="mr") take account
of missing marker genotype data.

> 2. Is there a way to estimate the effect of X-linked QTL based on
> multiple impumentation in r/qtl. I am aware that fitqtl can not
> currently handle X-linked data from an F2 intercross, but is there
> some
> work-around that you could suggest that would provide comparable
> results to those for autosomal QTL?

fitqtl should work for the X chromosome except for the coefficient
estimates (get.ests=TRUE).  I'm not sure how to code things in this
case.

> 3. I have used fitqtl to estimate the additive and dominant effect of
> autosomal QTL; however, I am not clear how the additive and dominant
> effects of QTL linked to dominant loci are estimated by fitqtl. Is
> estimation of additive and dominant effects for QTL linked to dominant
> loci dependent upon estimation of genotype probabilities based on
> linked codominant markers? If so, how should the fitqtl effect
> estimates for QTL from linkage groups with only dominant loci be
> interpreted?

You have exclusively dominant loci?  Are they all in the same phase, or
are there some with the A allele dominant and some with the B allele
dominant?

In fitqtl, we attempt to estimate the phenotypic averages for each of
the AA, AB, and BB groups and then turn these into additive and dominant
effects.  If you have exclusively dominant loci, it may not be possible
to separate the three underlying genotype groups, but this should be
reflected in the standard errors.

karl

messages.subject: Re: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.subject_clean: effect estimates with x-linked and dominant data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

Thanks for the note. Your reply regarding imputation and fitqtl clears
things up a bit. I had incorrectly thought that the analysis in
sim.geno was based on the analysis by calc.genoprob.

Below are follow-up questions on the other two poins.

> > 2. Is there a way to estimate the effect of X-linked QTL based on
> > multiple impumentation in r/qtl. I am aware that fitqtl can not
> > currently handle X-linked data from an F2 intercross, but is there
> > some
> > work-around that you could suggest that would provide comparable
> > results to those for autosomal QTL?
>
> fitqtl should work for the X chromosome except for the coefficient
> estimates (get.ests=TRUE).  I'm not sure how to code things in this
> case.

I am particularly interested in the coefficient estimates for the X
chromosome. Would it be valid to estimate the additive effect of
X-linked QTL by coding the A0 and B0 genotype classes as -1/2 and +1/2
in regression analysis as suggested by previous posts? If it is not
possible to do this with multiple imputation within r/qtl, would such
an analysis outside of r/qtl using the raw data provide comparable
results to those performed by fitqtl on autosomal data?

I am also considering estimating the additive effect of X-linked QTL
from the difference between phenotype means of AY and BY genotype
classes output from r/qtl (effectplot or scanone); however, I am not
clear how to estimate the standard error of the coefficient estimates
using this method.

> > 3. I have used fitqtl to estimate the additive and dominant effect of
> > autosomal QTL; however, I am not clear how the additive and dominant
> > effects of QTL linked to dominant loci are estimated by fitqtl. Is
> > estimation of additive and dominant effects for QTL linked to dominant
> > loci dependent upon estimation of genotype probabilities based on
> > linked codominant markers? If so, how should the fitqtl effect
> > estimates for QTL from linkage groups with only dominant loci be
> > interpreted?
>
> You have exclusively dominant loci?  Are they all in the same phase, or
> are there some with the A allele dominant and some with the B allele
> dominant?
>
> In fitqtl, we attempt to estimate the phenotypic averages for each of
> the AA, AB, and BB groups and then turn these into additive and dominant
> effects.  If you have exclusively dominant loci, it may not be possible
> to separate the three underlying genotype groups, but this should be
> reflected in the standard errors.

We have primarily dominant loci (both phases) and a handfull of
codominanat loci. We have two linkage maps, each composed of dominant
loci in phase and codominant loci, and analyze each map separately.
Most linkage groups contain several codominant loci, but a couple of
linkage groups do not contain any codominant loci.

I was concerned that the low information available to estimate genotype
for dominant loci unlinked to codominant loci would not be reflected in
the error associated with these coefficients; however, the standard
errors for the dominance effect estimate from fitqtl(get.ests=T) for
QTL on linkage groups with only dominant loci do appear to be higher
than those for QTL on linkage groups with codomiant loci as you
suggest.

Thanks again,
sky
